subject: Clearhaven — TTL exception process & artifacts for SOC 2
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearhaven.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: audit-team@clearhaven.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: TTL exceptions — ask + sample artifacts for SOC 2 audit

Hi Camila,

Quick follow-up from our SOC 2 prep: our auditors want to confirm how TTL exceptions are handled for short-lived tenants. Specifically:
- What is the documented process for requesting and approving a TTL extension/exception? (who approves, what justification fields)
- How is the exception recorded and for how long is the exception audit trail retained?
- Can you provide a small sampling of deletion run artifacts (proof that TTL exception was honored and deletion later occurred) — sample size 5 tenants across Nov–Oct window if possible.

They prefer: a human-readable runbook excerpt, the exception approval entry, and a sampling CSV with tenant id + timestamps + deletion-status. We understand redactions may be required for tenant names.

Can we get a first-pass packet by Monday? If not, can we carve out 30 minutes to walk through the orchestration and where artifacts live?

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Clearhaven — Head of Compliance Operations

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearhaven.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTL exceptions — ask + sample artifacts for SOC 2 audit

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask. We can supply the requested artifacts and a short walkthrough. Quick answers up front:
- Exception request flow: customer requests via Support portal -> Product Ops verifies scope -> Security authorizes exception if data residency or migration window required -> Legal signs off for >30-day extensions. Approvals are recorded in the exception registry with approver id, rationale, TTL override value, and expiration.
- Audit trail retention: exception registry entries and associated deletion/run logs are retained for 7 years by default for audit purposes; short-term operational logs (task queue traces) are retained 90 days.

I'll assemble a packet with: runbook excerpt, 5-row sampling CSV (tenant_id redacted -> tenant_hash, exception_request_ts, exception_expiry_ts, deletion_initiated_ts, deletion_completed_ts), and the registry approval copy (redacted).

If that timeline works we'll target delivery on Monday EOD PST. Would you like a 30-minute call Monday morning to walk the auditors through the places to verify records? Naomi and Vivek will join for infra/attestation detail.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
cc: naomi_feldman (Security), vivek_kulkarni (Platform)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTL exceptions — ask + sample artifacts for SOC 2 audit

On Sat, Nov 7, 2026 at 10:03 AM camila_reyes@redwood.com wrote:
> I'll assemble a packet with: runbook excerpt, 5-row sampling CSV (tenant_id redacted -> tenant_hash, exception_request_ts, exception_expiry_ts, deletion_initiated_ts, deletion_completed_ts), and the registry approval copy (redacted).

Adding technical notes for the packet and what we will attach:
1) redwood_ttl-exception_runbook_v1.pdf (attached stub) — excerpted pages 3–7 showing the approval workflow, automated orchestration steps, and the rollback criteria.
2) 2026-11-sampling-summary.csv (attached stub) — five anonymized tenant hashes with timestamps and final deletion_status (COMPLETED/FAILED + error codes if any).
3) Audit trail pointers — for each sample row we'll include the S3 object key (redacted) and a signed short-lived URL for auditors. We will also include a signed attestation link in the console for evidence playback.
4) Proof of retention policy application — logs showing registry entry creation, approver id, and TTL override value. (We will redact approver emails but include Redwood internal user IDs.)

Notes on scope/limitations: the operational task traces include ephemeral worker traces that are scrubbed after 90 days; the canonical evidence for deletion is the cloud lifecycle log + final object tombstone entry (retained per the 7-year attestation record). Some older tenants might have deletion procedures executed via our legacy deprovisioner; we'll flag those in the CSV and supply context.

I'll prepare the artifacts and provide a Drive link and the attestation URL by Monday. If auditors require signed csv exports (hashed), we can also provide a SHA256 checksum file.

— Vivek
Principal, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearhaven.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: audit-team@clearhaven.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTL exceptions — ask + sample artifacts for SOC 2 audit

Camila / Vivek —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Monday EOD for the packet is fine; the auditors asked for two small additions if possible:
- A short signed attestation from Redwood that the sampling CSV rows correspond to canonical deletion artifacts (a link to your attestation console with a requestor-signed statement will work).
- A brief note in the runbook excerpt about how we handle TTL exceptions created during active data migrations (this is a specific audit focus area).

We can take the Drive link + attestation URL and replay during our Tuesday audit call. Please include any checksum files for the CSV.

Thanks again,
Liam
Clearhaven — Head of Compliance Operations
